media.title: Rue Alphonse-de-Neuville, Paris — historical postcard
media.description: Early twentieth-century postcard view of rue Alphonse-de-Neuville in the Plaine Monceau quarter of Paris. It provides period street context for the Polish Consulate General, located at number 19 in the late 1920s and 1930s; the postcard does not establish that the consulate building itself is visible.
media.altText: Early twentieth-century postcard showing rue Alphonse-de-Neuville in Paris, lined with town houses, with horse-drawn carriages and pedestrians.
media.publicCaption: Rue Alphonse-de-Neuville in the Plaine Monceau quarter of Paris, early twentieth century. The Polish Consulate General was located at number 19 in the late 1920s and 1930s.

places.publicNote: Polish consular institution in Paris that issued Kaper’s Polish passport in August 1934, later noted in the Calexico border-crossing documentation. Historical address identified as 19 rue Alphonse-de-Neuville, Paris 17e.
